name: Shillong
description: Capital of Meghalaya and headquarters of East Khasi Hills district, known as the Scotland of the East. A scenic hill station at about 1,500 m elevation with pine-covered hills, colonial architecture, markets, and a base for exploring surrounding waterfalls, peaks, and cultural sites.
facts: Headquarters of East Khasi Hills and state capital
Named after the deity Lei Shyllong
Main base for trips to Cherrapunji and nearby attractions

name: Shillong Peak
description: Highest peak in Meghalaya at about 1,965 m, located about 10 km from Shillong city. Offers panoramic views of the city, surrounding hills, and valleys; popular for sunsets and photography. Features a small sanctum dedicated to U Lei Shillong.
facts: Panoramic views of the city and countryside
Sacred site for local Khasi traditions

name: Elephant Falls
description: Three-tiered waterfall about 12 km from Shillong, locally known as Ka Kshaid Lai Pateng Khohsiew. Cascades through fern-covered rocks in a scenic forested setting, easily accessible with viewing points for each tier.
facts: Named after an elephant-shaped rock at the base

name: Ward's Lake
description: Man-made colonial-era lake in central Shillong, locally known as Nan Polok. Features a picturesque arched bridge, flower gardens, gravel paths, and boating facilities, named after Sir William Ward.
facts: Also called Pollock's Lake or Nan Polok
Artificial lake with walking paths and gardens
Located in the heart of Shillong

name: Don Bosco Centre for Indigenous Cultures
description: Major museum in Mawlai, Shillong, showcasing the cultures, arts, crafts, and lifestyles of indigenous peoples of Northeast India. Features multiple galleries in a unique multi-storey building with research facilities.
facts: Also known as Don Bosco Museum
Focuses on indigenous cultures of Northeast India

name: Sohra (Cherrapunji)
description: Subdivisional town in East Khasi Hills, historically one of the wettest places on Earth. Gateway to numerous waterfalls, caves, and living root bridges, set on a plateau overlooking the plains of Bangladesh.
facts: Formerly known as Cherrapunjee or Cherrapunji
Once the wettest place on Earth
Base for Nohkalikai Falls and living root bridges

name: Nohkalikai Falls
description: Tallest plunge waterfall in India at about 340 m (1,115 ft), located near Sohra. Drops from a plateau edge into a turquoise pool, fed by rainfall on the Cherrapunji plateau; associated with a local Khasi legend.
facts: Named after the legend of Ka Likai

name: Nohsngithiang Falls (Seven Sisters Falls)
description: Segmented waterfall near Mawsmai village, dropping about 315 m in multiple streams over limestone cliffs. Also known as Seven Sisters Falls; offers views toward the Bangladesh plains, best in monsoon.
facts: Also called Seven Sisters Waterfalls or Mawsmai Falls

name: Mawsmai Cave
description: Accessible limestone cave near Sohra with lit passages, stalactites, and stalagmites. About 150 m long, one of the most visitor-friendly caves in Meghalaya, located near Nohsngithiang Falls.
facts: Near Sohra and Seven Sisters Falls

name: Double Decker Living Root Bridge (Nongriat)
description: Iconic two-tiered living root bridge in Nongriat village near Sohra, formed by guided growth of Ficus elastica aerial roots. Requires a steep trek of about 3,500 steps from Tyrna; UNESCO tentative list feature of Khasi bio-engineering.
facts: Made from living rubber tree roots
Near Sohra in East Khasi Hills

name: Mawlynnong Village
description: Village in Pynursla block known as the cleanest village in Asia. Features living root bridges, skywalks, orchids, and community-led cleanliness; located near the India-Bangladesh border about 90 km from Shillong.
facts: Declared cleanest village in Asia by Discover India
Known for living root bridges and skyview

name: Laitlum Canyon
description: Dramatic canyon viewpoint about 25 km from Shillong near Smit, offering sweeping views of deep valleys, ridges, and distant plains. Popular for photography, short walks, and panoramic landscapes.
facts: Also known as Laitlum Grand Canyon or Smit Valley viewpoint

name: Mawphlang Sacred Forest
description: Ancient sacred grove about 25 km from Shillong, preserved by Khasi traditions as the abode of local deities. Features old trees, orchids, and biodiversity; no removal of anything allowed under local customs.
facts: Home to rare plants and orchids

name: Arwah Cave
description: Limestone cave near Sohra with marine fossils, large chambers, and natural formations. Accessible via a short walk, offering a wilder caving experience compared to Mawsmai, with views of surrounding gorges.

name: Kongthong Village (Whistling Village)
description: Remote village in East Khasi Hills known for the unique whistled language Jingrwai Iawbei, where individuals are identified by melodies. Features living root bridges and panoramic hill views; about 60 km from Shillong.
facts: Known as the Singing or Whistling Village
Nominated for UNWTO Best Tourism Villages
